newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 27.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton rejected opposition allegations that the ruling coalition was divided over policy towards the Irish Republican Army's (IRA) political wing, Sinn Fein.
- Waterford Foods Board has agreed to accept an improved merger offer from Avonmore Foods Plc worth 337 million Irish pounds.
- The French Prime Minister, Alan Juppe has announced his resignation.
- A merger of Irish food giants Waterford Foods and Avonmore Foods Plc appeared on the cards last night after Waterford's board accepted an improved merger offer.
- The opposition Fianna Fail party is to intensify efforts to capitalise as what it sees as a serious government split on Sinn Fein
- Nearly 500 candidates plan to contest election to the 166 parliamentary seats in June 6 elections.
- Prime Minister John Bruton and Foreign Minister Dick Spring are playing down differences over Sinn Fein.
- Avonmore Foods Plc has boosted its offer for Waterford Foods.
- The Progresive Democrats opposition party backed away from a policy of shedding public service jobs after its ally, Fianna Fail, said it would not go along with the strategy.
